$comment: DERIVED, not verbatim. Written by this library from the prose of RFC 9162. Source .cache/rfc-9162.txt (RFC 9162, Certificate Transparency Version 2.0, sha256 a0e432ce7580c99fcc8faf0cf3f6191f9ce6b4864f949158e020d4ecb295081f). RFC 9162 Section 5 gives these messages in prose and ships no JSON Schema. INSTANCE: the 2xx JSON response of get-anchors (Section 5.7). certificates is an array of base64 CA certificates. max_chain_length is the maximum number of certificates in the chain 'in decimal' and omitted when there is no limit; the source does not say whether this JSON member is a number or a decimal string, so both are accepted (SOURCE AMBIGUITY) and nothing else is. Instances are JSON values as received; binary fields stay base64 text and are not decoded (RFC 4648 Section 4, per Section 5). A pattern ^AQ[...] on a TransItem field binds the first two decoded octets, the VersionedTransType code of Section 4.5, because base64 of 0x01 0x0T begins AQ (every code here has 0 in its high nibble) and the low nibble T confines the third character to a block of four, its other two bits coming from the next octet; hence four characters per code in each pattern. The pattern states what a v2 log emits; it is not a client acceptance test, since a v2 client MUST NOT construe a non-v2 SCT (rfc-9162#R-0069) or an unrecognized TransItem type (rfc-9162#R-0079) as an error. Fields the RFC does not define are allowed (Section 5: any fields not understood SHOULD be ignored). A constraint marked inferred is a reading this library made, not a statement of the source. This schema cannot check the TransItem body, signatures, or any cross-field relation: those are in ../messages.yaml (constrained_by and notes per field).
